title: Tiered SLO Targets (Working Sheet) — Hosted vs Dedicated
content:
DOC NOTE (working sheet): This is the SRE/PM working table for proposed SLO targets by endpoint, tier, and region. Values are proposals pending final approval in PM-812. Assumes tier tags are correct at ingest and persist through routing/fallback (see ENG-4922).

Last updated: 2026-02-14 by Aisha (notes incorporated from Product + Routing review).

========================
TAB: Overview / Conventions
========================
Reporting window (SLO compliance): Rolling 28 days (monthly-style) unless explicitly noted.

Primary SLIs:
1) Availability / Success rate: good_requests / total_valid_requests
   - good_requests: HTTP 2xx/3xx AND (for streaming) clean stream completion OR server-acknowledged end-of-stream
   - bad_requests counted against SLO: 5xx, gateway timeouts, upstream timeouts, server-side stream disconnects, internal routing failures
   - excluded from denominator: invalid requests (4xx), auth failures (401/403), explicit rate limiting (429), customer-canceled (client abort) when we have positive client-abort signal

2) Latency: end-to-end request latency measured at API gateway ingress to first byte (TTFB) and/or complete response
   - Non-streaming: total request duration (ingress -> response complete)
   - Streaming: TTFB and steady-state token streaming reliability tracked separately; completion time is not a customer-friendly SLI (highly prompt/token dependent)

3) Streaming reliability: stream_disconnect_rate = server_disconnect_events / total_streams
   - server_disconnect_event means stream ended without proper end marker AND NOT classified as client abort

Important notes on trade-offs:
- Hosted is shared capacity: targets need to be achievable under burst traffic with overload protection + graceful degradation (routing/fallback, admission control) without constant release freezes.
- Dedicated should have tighter latency + availability, but must be backed by explicit headroom and fleet escalation playbooks. Dedicated “global” is not assumed; SLOs are per contracted region.
- p99 targets are the hardest; they drive queueing/capacity policy. p95 is the primary customer perceived “feels fast” metric.

Measurement granularity:
- Default: tier x region x endpoint_class.
- Avoid per-model / per-customer high-cardinality breakdown in SLO computation. Provide separate dashboards for “top contributors” using sampling/aggregation.

========================
TAB: Proposed Targets (Table)
========================
Columns:
- endpoint_class: chat_completions | chat_completions_streaming | completions | embeddings
- measurement: availability | latency_p95_ms | latency_p99_ms | streaming_disconnect_rate
- tier: hosted | dedicated
- region: us-east-1 | us-west-2 | eu-west-1 | eu-central-1
- slo_target: target value
- reporting_window: 28d
- feasibility: green | yellow | red
- notes: rationale / known risks / dependencies

TABLE (proposed)
| endpoint_class | measurement | tier | region | slo_target | reporting_window | feasibility | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| chat_completions | availability | hosted | us-east-1 | 99.90% | 28d | yellow | Requires routing fallback to compatible hosted models during pool saturation; must ensure fallback errors count correctly. Recent burst incidents show we dip to 99.7–99.85% without tighter overload shedding. |
| chat_completions | availability | hosted | us-west-2 | 99.90% | 28d | yellow | Similar to us-east-1. Depend on admission control + cache effectiveness; avoid throttling via 429 (excluded) becoming de facto outage. |
| chat_completions | availability | hosted | eu-west-1 | 99.85% | 28d | yellow | EU has more frequent capacity constraints + longer tail due to cross-AZ variance; proposed slightly lower vs US until fleet headroom improves. |
| chat_completions | availability | hosted | eu-central-1 | 99.85% | 28d | red | Current regional maturity lower; paging noise expected. Consider phased ramp: start at 99.7% then tighten after Q2 capacity adds. |
| chat_completions | latency_p95_ms | hosted | us-east-1 | 900 | 28d | yellow | Measured as ingress->response complete for non-stream. p95 sensitive to batching + queue. Requires tighter max queue time at router. |
| chat_completions | latency_p95_ms | hosted | us-west-2 | 950 | 28d | yellow | Slightly higher due to observed west tail. If we keep equal across US, expect more budget burn in us-west-2. |
| chat_completions | latency_p95_ms | hosted | eu-west-1 | 1200 | 28d | yellow | Customer expectation in EU is “slower but stable”. Needs router regional pinning improvements to avoid cross-region spill. |
| chat_completions | latency_p95_ms | hosted | eu-central-1 | 1300 | 28d | red | High variance today; depends on fleet maturity + reducing cold-starts. |
| chat_completions | latency_p99_ms | hosted | us-east-1 | 2500 | 28d | red | p99 is dominated by queue spikes + rare kernel regressions. Expect burn during deploys unless deploy gate + canaries are in place. |
| chat_completions | latency_p99_ms | hosted | us-west-2 | 2700 | 28d | red | Same risk as us-east-1. Consider tracking p99 as secondary (dashboard-only) initially; enforcement only after burn-rate alert tuning. |
| chat_completions | latency_p99_ms | hosted | eu-west-1 | 3500 | 28d | red | Tail is worse; may require prioritized scheduling for interactive traffic. |
| chat_completions | latency_p99_ms | hosted | eu-central-1 | 4000 | 28d | red | Not currently realistic without headroom; propose phase-in. |

| chat_completions_streaming | availability | hosted | eu-central-1 | 99.80% | 28d | red | Too many ambiguous disconnects today; fix taxonomy + tracing propagation first. |
| chat_completions_streaming | latency_p95_ms | hosted | us-east-1 | 450 (TTFB) | 28d | yellow | Streaming latency target is TTFB. Needs prefix caching improvements and router pre-allocation. |

| chat_completions_streaming | latency_p95_ms | hosted | eu-west-1 | 650 (TTFB) | 28d | yellow | Validate with customer telemetry; ensure we measure first-byte consistently at gateway. |

| chat_completions_streaming | latency_p99_ms | hosted | us-west-2 | 1400 (TTFB) | 28d | red | Same as us-east-1. |

| embeddings | availability | hosted | us-east-1 | 99.95% | 28d | green | Embeddings path is simpler (no streaming) and more batch-friendly. Most failures are gateway/upstream timeouts. |

| embeddings | availability | hosted | eu-west-1 | 99.90% | 28d | yellow | EU pool smaller; careful with spillover behavior. |

---
DEDICATED TIER (per contracted region; no cross-region spill unless explicitly configured)
---
| chat_completions | availability | dedicated | us-east-1 | 99.95% | 28d | yellow | Must be backed by headroom commitments and fleet escalation (see capacity mitigation notes). Dedicated should not rely on hosted shared fallback by default. |
| chat_completions | availability | dedicated | us-west-2 | 99.95% | 28d | yellow | Similar. |

========================
TAB: Notes / Open Questions / Decisions Needed
========================
1) Hosted EU targets
- Decision needed: do we standardize hosted availability across regions (simpler) or acknowledge region maturity (more accurate)? Current table proposes slightly lower in EU.

2) p99 enforcement strategy
- Proposal: track p99 in dashboards for all tiers, but only use p95 for budget enforcement in phase 1 for Hosted (warn-only for p99 burn signals). Dedicated can enforce both earlier because it’s contract-adjacent.
- Risk: customers often cite “p99 pain” even when p95 looks fine.

3) Streaming accounting
- Blocking: consistent client abort detection across SDKs; otherwise disconnect_rate is noisy and may lead to unnecessary freezes.
- Action: align event taxonomy with Observability Standards and confirm gateway emits explicit abort reason codes.

4) Fallback behavior and SLI attribution
- Hosted fallback to compatible models is expected for resiliency; Dedicated fallback should be opt-in + contractual.
- Need to confirm: when fallback occurs, do we attribute latency to original policy or actual model? (should be actual, but tie-break for customer-facing explanation.)

5) Metric coverage + cardinality
- Must ensure tier, endpoint_class, region labels exist on all required metrics before publishing targets.
- Avoid per-customer labels in SLO computation; dedicated customer dashboards should be separate queries with access controls.

6) Suggested next steps
- Review meeting: SRE + PM Hosted + PM Dedicated + Routing (Mina) to finalize values and highlight red rows as phase-in candidates.
- After approval: implement SLO config schema entries per tier/region/endpoint and wire burn-rate alerts; then tune thresholds before turning on hard deploy gates.

Owner notes to self (Aisha):
- Re-check embeddings p99 in EU after routing changes land (recent queue behavior improved in staging).
- Confirm whether we need separate targets for /v1/responses vs /v1/chat/completions (currently rolled up as chat_completions).
- Cross-check with Dedicated SLA mapping draft once it’s stable; ensure we don’t promise a tighter SLA than we can enforce with error budgets.
